The merge step of merge sort. Records are compared by `rec[0]` only, and the sort must be stable:

```
def merge(left, right):
    out, i, j = [], 0, 0
    while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
        if left[i][0] ____ right[j][0]:
            out.append(left[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            out.append(right[j])
            j += 1
    return out + left[i:] + right[j:]
```

Every comparison-based sort needs Ω(n log n) comparisons in the worst case. What is the core of the proof?
options: A decision tree that sorts must have at least n! leaves, so its height is at least log2(n!) = Θ(n log n)

text: Radix sort can sort `n` fixed-width integers in O(n) time. Why doesn't this contradict the Ω(n log n) lower bound?
